blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Cybersecurity in practice is a steady discipline, not an annual training. It is the small habits, repeated daily by everyone, that block almost all realistic attacks: strong passwords, two-factor authentication, careful clicking, locked screens, reported suspicions, patched software and clean backups.

A good intermediate security programme has two parts. The technical part — the tools, the monitoring, the incident response — is usually handled by the security team. The human part — the daily habits of everyone else — is where most incidents are actually won or lost, and that part is everyone's responsibility.

Every employee must be treated as part of the security team, even if they do not think of themselves that way. When culture is right, technology rarely has to save the day. When culture is wrong, even the best technology eventually fails.

items.q: According to the text, what blocks almost all realistic attacks?
options: The work of the security team alone
Small habits repeated daily by everyone
items.why: "the small habits, repeated daily by everyone, that block almost all realistic attacks."

items.q: Who usually handles the technical part of the programme?
items.why: "The technical part… is usually handled by the security team."

items.q: According to the text, where are most incidents actually won or lost?
options: In the daily habits of everyone else
items.why: "The human part — the daily habits of everyone else — is where most incidents are actually won or lost."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Good technology cannot fully replace good habits.
Careful clicking is part of practical security.
A yearly training course is enough to keep a company safe.
items.why: Inferência: o texto abre dizendo que segurança "is a steady discipline, not an annual training" — o treinamento anual sozinho não basta.

items.q: What does the contrast between the last two sentences suggest?
options: Technology should be replaced by culture
Culture matters more than the quality of the tools
items.why: Inferência: com cultura certa a tecnologia raramente precisa agir; com cultura errada até a melhor tecnologia falha — a cultura pesa mais.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte no lembrete semanal de segurança para a equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Morning, everyone. It's Charlotte, with your one-minute security nudge for the week. No training slides today — just one habit to keep alive.

This week it's about links. If an email pushes you to act fast, click a strange link, or reset a password you didn't ask to change, that pressure is the warning sign. It should be paused, not obeyed. Nothing needs to be forwarded to prove it's real; the message can simply be reported to the security team, and they'll take it from there.

And please — you don't have to be certain. If something feels slightly off, it should still be reported. We would far rather look at ten harmless emails than miss the one that matters. Nobody here will ever be blamed for flagging a false alarm.

One last thing before you get back to it: two-factor authentication must stay switched on, even when it's annoying. That extra step is often the only thing standing between a stolen password and a real breach. That's it — same time next week. Thanks, all.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is this week's security nudge about?
options: Suspicious links and pressure to act fast
items.why: "This week it's about links. If an email pushes you to act fast, click a strange link…"

items.q: What does Charlotte say you should do with a suspicious message?
options: Report it to the security team
Reply and ask who sent it
Forward it to prove it is real
items.why: "the message can simply be reported to the security team, and they'll take it from there."

items.q: According to Charlotte, what should you do if you are not certain something is dangerous?
options: Ignore it, to avoid false alarms
Ask a colleague to decide for you
Wait until you are sure before doing anything
items.why: "you don't have to be certain. If something feels slightly off, it should still be reported."

items.q: What does Charlotte suggest by saying nobody will be blamed for flagging a false alarm?
options: Only the security team may report emails
False alarms are a serious problem for the team
She wants people to feel safe reporting, so real threats aren't missed
Reporting is optional and rarely useful
items.why: Inferência: ao remover o medo de errar, ela incentiva o hábito de reportar — melhor dez falsos alarmes do que perder o e-mail que importa.

items.q: Why does Charlotte insist that two-factor authentication stay on, even when it is annoying?
options: Because it often is the last barrier before a real breach
Because it is required by the annual training
Because it speeds up logging in
items.why: Inferência: ela chama o passo extra de "the only thing standing between a stolen password and a real breach" — a incomodação vale o risco evitado.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Security is a steady discipline, not a one-off event." A steady discipline is…
options: a consistent practice kept up over time
a set of formal written rules
items.why: Steady discipline = disciplina constante: algo praticado com regularidade ao longo do tempo.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Even with a strong password, ___ adds a second step that a thief usually cannot pass."
items.why: Two-factor authentication = autenticação em dois fatores, o segundo passo além da senha.

items.q: "The team's incident response was fast." Incident response is…
options: the plan for handling a security event once it happens
items.why: Incident response = resposta a incidentes: como a equipe age quando um problema de fato ocorre.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Attackers often exploit old bugs, so ___ closes doors before anyone tries them."
items.why: Patched software = software atualizado: corrige falhas conhecidas antes que sejam exploradas.

items.q: "Good monitoring caught the login from an unusual country." Monitoring is…
options: watching systems to spot unusual activity
items.why: Monitoring = monitoramento: observar os sistemas para detectar atividade fora do padrão.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em reuniões de segurança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The security lead still has to sign off on the new policy." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out two-factor authentication team by team." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "If an email feels wrong, flag it to the security team." To flag something means to…
items.why: Flag = sinalizar, chamar a atenção para algo suspeito.

items.q: "Everyone agreed to lock their screens, but few followed through." They…
options: did not carry it out in practice
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim, cumprir na prática o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Reminding people once a year won't move the needle on real behaviour." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
